introduction: Legal Aid Services of Oregon routes legal-help requests by county. Its directory also links other legal-aid organizations where LASO is not the local provider.
description: Legal Aid Services of Oregon routes legal-help requests by county. Its directory also links other legal-aid organizations where LASO is not the local provider.

sections.who: The provider serves low-income people with qualifying legal problems. Intake screens the issue, location and financial circumstances.
sections.get: Help can address civil issues including housing, benefits and consumer problems, depending on the case and available service.
sections.docs:
• County and contact information.
  • Income details requested at intake.
  • Court papers, notices and dates.
sections.apply:
1. Select your county

    Use LASO’s office directory.

  2. Follow local intake instructions

    Contact the listed provider; a county link may lead to Oregon Law Center or Oregon Law Help.

  3. Describe any deadline

    Tell intake staff about eviction papers or hearings and supply requested records.
sections.after: Clarify whether representation has been accepted. Follow court instructions while waiting for an intake decision.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using County intake routes, Services and eviction referral. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: Does every county go to LASO?
No. Its county directory routes some areas to other legal-aid providers.
What if I have eviction court papers?
LASO’s homepage directs people with eviction papers to the Eviction Defense Project.
Does contacting an office establish representation?
Ask the provider directly whether it has accepted your case.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
